item.title: nixos/wrappers: migrate to use overlayfs
item.description:
Our C wrappers are a disaster.

  • they attempt to do env filtering (a fools errand)
  • they are written against static musl
    • supposedly more secure
    • pulls a bunch of musl stuff into the default system closure
    • musl got its last release in march, before that in 2024, which does not invoke confidence
  • capability wrappers do not propagate AT_SECURE
  • capability wrappers lift all capabilities into ambient set
    • this makes further execs more privileged than programs may expect
  • the wrapper code was C mostly written in 2016 with little review since

We can do better. We don't actually need C wrappers at all. Rather, we can just build an overlayfs to reuse nix store paths as targets, but apply dedicated metadata (suid/sgid/caps) via overlayfs. It isn't even too hard to retrofit overlayfs into the existing machinery. Instead of writing a wrapper binary directly, write an empty file and apply the metadata, then use that in a metacopy overlayfs to make it work.

This should alleviate a good chunk of the security concerns, while not running into the limitations i ran into trying to go one step further and build the metadata as erofs.

item.title: goose-cli, goose-desktop: 1.49.0 -> 1.53.0
item.description:
Bumps both goose packages from 1.49.0 to 1.53.0.

Changelog: https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/releases/tag/v1.53.0

goose-cli

  • new src tarball hash + cargoHash
  • two pre-existing tests now need sandbox skips:
    • command_runs_with_configured_cwd_and_resolves_relative_path: test body changed in upstream #11501 to symlink /bin/pwd, which does not exist in the Nix sandbox /bin (only sh)
    • relay_to_direct_upgrade_loses_no_data: performs real iroh holepunching over loopback with a 30s deadline; times out under the sandbox's restricted networking (test and crate code unchanged between 1.49.0 and 1.53.0)

goose-desktop

  • the @aaif/goose-sdk UI workspace was replaced by @aaif/goose-acp-client in 1.53.0; the pre-packaging build step now builds goose-acp-client instead of sdk
  • new pnpmDeps hash

Verified on NixOS x86_64-linux: both packages build; the goose-cli cargo test suite runs green in checkPhase (2511 passed, 2 sandbox skips); goose --version reports 1.53.0; desktop version also runs.

AI disclosure (per the automation/AI policy): the package.nix changes, their verification, and this summary were produced with the assistance of the LLM-based agent goose (AAIF) running the qwen3.8-27B model. The submitter reviewed the diff, the build/test results, and this description before submission; the commit carries an Assisted-by: trailer.

fixed 20 cves, among other things. full changelog: https://downloads.apache.org/httpd/CHANGES_2.4.69

  • CVE-2026-93546: mod_dav_fs namespace overflow
  • CVE-2026-79768: mod_userdir information disclosure
  • CVE-2026-73637: mod_auth_digest DoS attack
  • CVE-2026-73636: mod_auth_digest one-time-nonce replay attack
  • CVE-2026-63718: mod_proxy_uwsgi Transfer-Encoding response smuggling
  • CVE-2026-63686: mod_xml2enc crash on charset conversion failure
  • CVE-2026-63292: mod_vhost_alias stack overflow
  • CVE-2026-63045: mod_proxy_ftp PASV address handling
  • CVE-2026-59797: mod_ssl SSLRequire allows .htaccess ap_expr file-function
  • CVE-2026-59685: Out-of-Bounds Write in ap_directory_walk() Canonical-Name Rewrite on CASE_BLIND_FILESYSTEM
  • CVE-2026-58415: mod_dav_fs property database read access
  • CVE-2026-57941: mod_http2 use-after-free / wild write via shared session->bbtmp re-entrancy
  • CVE-2026-56449: mod_proxy_html: crash in dump_content
  • CVE-2026-56154: mod_rewrite use-after-free via %{LA-U:HTTP:...}
  • CVE-2026-56153: mod_charset_lite: Heap overflow in finish_partial_char
  • CVE-2026-48005: mod_auth_digest reauthentication attack
  • CVE-2026-47360: mod_session: Session cookie not removed during internal redirect
  • CVE-2026-46729: mod_heartmonitor denial of service
  • CVE-2026-42528: mod_dav shared lock overflow
  • CVE-2026-42356: limited RCE for some internal redirects to non-CGI files in CGI directories
